messages.author: 6e4e10e46624db56
messages.subject: Inverse Ditance for Besag Prior
parts:
Dear INLA Forum

I  would like to ask how we can use inverse distance weight matrix for Besag prior. As I know the "graph" in Besag prior is an adjacency matrix. It is binary matrix. Here I would like to use the actual distance instead of Binary W. 

Thank you very much

Best regards
Mindra

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Inverse Ditance for Besag Prior
parts:
You can do this manually, using the model 'generic0'; see

inla.doc("generic0")

make sure to scale the model; see the vignette about scaling, and you
have to add the argument, diagonal=1e-4 , f.ex, in case your model is
intrinsic.

H

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Inverse Ditance for Besag Prior
parts:
Historical note:
Applying inverse distance weighting to the complete graph is likely not very useful (dense matrix etc), but inverse distance weighting on a small neighbourhood is one of the old methods for constructing GMRFs on graphs, and it's not necessarily universally better or worse than binary weighting for those same neighbours; in the case of a regular hexagonal grid it's the same thing. But just as binary weighting isn't consistent between different spatial discretisations, neither is inverse distance weighting. In contrast, the "cotangent of adjacent/opposing angles" method is another approach, that turned out to be what the SPDE finite element construction also involves, so it at least has some kind of consistency properties, even though the direct equivalence is for the 1st order case that has a generalised random field as limit (it's the elements of the "G" matrix) so the interpretation isn't straightforward.

Finn

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: Re: Inverse Ditance for Besag Prior
parts:
Hi Mindra,

As far as I know, it is not easy to choose an appropriate inverse distance weight matrix for Besag models. It requires to meet several conditions(you may read the paper (SAR and CAR) from Jay M. Ver Hoef.). Further, when you visualize your graph using INLA code, it looks strange. There is also some discussion in this forum, such as (the title) "Can INLA utilise a non-symmetric adjacency matrix?"

Hope this helps.
Yuheng
